name: manual_17fce3
claim: Across a long arc of successive CodeRabbit review rounds on the same evolving PR, a consistent minority of findings are stale (already fixed by intervening work, or describing code that no longer matches the cited lines) and should be verified against current code and skipped with a documented reason rather than blindly re-applied. The majority that are genuinely valid split into two useful categories: findings that are proportionate to fix immediately (a local, well-scoped correctness bug), and findings whose literal ask is disproportionate to the current PR's scope (e.g. "make this schema hard-required across two repositories in the same session" when one of the repositories has no equivalent system to enforce it against) -- for the latter, implement the safer, backward-compatible version of the same underlying concern (optional-and-validated instead of hard-required) and explicitly flag the disproportionate part for the operator's decision rather than either ignoring it or unilaterally implementing the large version.

decisions.notes: Meta-lesson tying together the whole multi-round review discipline across this arc.

rationale: Meta-lesson tying together the whole multi-round review discipline across this arc.
